source_review.notes: Checked current Linux documentation for process address spaces and page tables, current Linux man-pages for fork, clone, exec, mmap, mprotect, proc maps, credentials, PID namespaces, pidfds, and waiting, plus MIT's 2025 xv6 text. All 13 cited URLs returned HTTP 200; Linux-specific representations and APIs are attributed rather than treated as universal OS contracts.

evidence: Checked VMA set V, intervals v_i, starts s_i, ends e_i, address a, operation op, page size P, vpn, offset o, pfn, frames f and g, references, and process lifetime tuple for definition before use.
Reviewed process, thread, address space, VMA, page table, TLB, copy-on-write, PID, namespace, pidfd, zombie, and reaping terminology against cited sources.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation distinguishes virtual range policy, current translation, physical backing, logical sharing, and namespace-scoped lifetime identity.

evidence: Executed the copy-on-write model and confirmed frame 7 reference count rises from one to two when the child mapping is copied.
Confirmed the child write decrements frame 7 to one owner, creates frame 8 with one owner and value B, and leaves the parent's frame 7 value A unchanged.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic one-page example demonstrates reference and value separation without claiming page-table, concurrency, or allocation behavior.

evidence: Re-derived the half-open VMA validity and adjacent nonoverlap conditions and checked virtual address decomposition into vpn and page offset under positive page size P.
Checked physical address reconstruction pfn times P plus offset and the COW transition from two references on f to one on f and one on copied frame g.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The translation equation is explicitly conditional on valid mappings, present page-table state, privileges, and permissions; huge mappings alter level and offset width.

evidence: Reviewed gaps, half-open endpoints, overflow, fixed mappings, permission changes, nonresident pages, concurrent fault and unmap, COW double writers, allocation failure, migration, pinning, and TLB invalidation.

Reviewed multithreaded exec and exit, inherited descriptors, PID and pointer reuse, nested PID namespaces, zombie retention, raced proc observations, writable-executable pages, inspection authority, and resource exhaustion.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Mapping, translation, sharing, concurrency, identity, authority, lifecycle, observation, security, and safety boundaries receive separate treatment.

evidence: Traced identity, mapping, translation, sharing, COW, authority, lifecycle, and evidence integrity through exposition, ten examples, and five answers.
Verified the executable model preserves one mapping per address-space page, balances references after the split, and changes only the child's logical value.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter never equates process with program, VMA with page-table entry, virtual size with residency, descriptor copies with resource copies, or exit with reaping.

evidence: Reviewed the process-reference-graph argument across threads, address spaces, files, credentials, signals, namespaces, limits, and parentage.
Constructed counterexamples for PID reuse, virtual-to-physical contiguity inference, VMA-only stabilization, unsynchronized thread unmap, exec-as-new-process, and zombie-as-running-process.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides reusable representation and lifecycle obligations, not a formal proof of Linux memory management, hardware translation, or process isolation.

evidence: Audited uses of valid, successful, correct, safe, exactly once, stable, isolate, prove, and certification.
Confirmed abstract interval and COW relations, Linux implementation claims, executable observations, diagnostic metrics, and human assurance remain differently scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: VMA eligibility is explicitly necessary but insufficient for hardware access, and stable pidfds are not claimed to freeze mutable process state.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-011/report.json records the exact three-line output for toy-copy-on-write under Python 3.
Reviewed proc maps, resident metrics, fault tests, concurrency, TLB, interference, security, and safety passages for snapshot, implementation, workload, and coverage limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing dictionary model excludes page tables, TLBs, concurrent faults, allocation failure, shared mappings, huge pages, files, signals, security, and a real fork.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed program image, process, thread, resource domains, address spaces, mappings, translations, sharing, identities, authority, termination, and observation as distinct but coupled concepts.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed VMAs, page tables, faults, mapping permissions, COW, clone sharing, exec replacement, PIDs and pidfds, descriptors, signals, concurrency, reaping, proc observations, and limits as implementable concerns. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from process reference graph through address-space mechanics, sharing and identity to exit and security, followed by seven trade-offs, fourteen misconceptions, ten examples, and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, Linux-memory-management-maintainer, kernel-practitioner, hardware, concurrency, security, real-time, safety, or certification review is claimed.
